purpose: Estimate evidential independence of machine-psychology findings instead of treating publication count or citation count as replication count.
epistemic_warning: Scores produced by this engine are evidence-maturity metrics, not probabilities that a psychological interpretation is true.

unit_of_analysis.report: one empirical paper or independently analyzable experiment family
unit_of_analysis.research_group: author/lab cluster with material personnel or institutional continuity
unit_of_analysis.benchmark_family: tests descended from substantially the same task/template/scoring lineage
unit_of_analysis.evidence_line: a report or cluster contributing non-redundant evidence to a narrowly defined claim

pairwise_redundancy_dimensions.measure: weighted author-set overlap; core-author overlap counts more than peripheral overlap
shared primary lab/institution or directly continuous team
same model/product family and materially similar checkpoint/version
same benchmark, questionnaire, task template or direct derivative
same evaluation/training dataset or direct sample derivative
same prompts/templates or lightly modified descendants
same evaluation implementation/codebase or direct fork
direct follow-up, reproduction or method transfer from the compared report

pairwise_formula.bounds_rule: For UNKNOWN overlap, compute conservative lower independence assuming shared and upper independence assuming independent. UNKNOWN must never silently become zero overlap.

pairwise_classes.criterion: 0.25 <= independence_upper_bound < 0.50 or strong known shared lineage
bounds cross multiple classes because metadata is missing

effective_evidence_count.formula: N_eff = (sum_i w_i)^2 / sum_i sum_j (w_i * w_j * R_ij), with R_ii=1 and R_ij=redundancy_ij
effective_evidence_count.bounds: Compute N_eff_low using conservative UNKNOWN overlaps and N_eff_high using optimistic UNKNOWN overlaps.
effective_evidence_count.interpretation: N_eff approximates how many fully independent equally weighted evidence lines would contain comparable non-redundant information.

claim_maturity.rule: A high maturity score supports the narrowly operationalized claim only. It cannot upgrade behavioral evidence into subjective experience, intrinsic personality or consciousness.

non_independence_penalties.same_model_only: small-to-moderate penalty; model replication still informs reproducibility but not cross-model generality

anti_double_counting_rules: A survey does not count as an empirical replication of the papers it summarizes.
A benchmark paper reusing source-paper examples does not become fully independent merely by testing more models.
A paper containing many experiments contributes multiple evidence lines only when experiments have materially independent datasets/tasks and are not pseudo-replicates.
A model-version comparison within one paper is model-diversity evidence, not multiple research-group replications.
A direct mitigation study can support manipulability without independently confirming the proposed causal mechanism.
Citation count contributes zero direct replication weight.
